name: psychological_level_mean_reversion_5s
author: adapted from Gemini Quant
thesis: Exploits round-number bias. Retail stop-loss orders and limit orders cluster at levels like 500, 1000, 1500. This creates artificial resistance/support. Price often 'pierces' these levels to hunt liquidity and then reverts. This is a behavioral constraint of retail-heavy markets like India.
mechanism: Order flow imbalance between aggressive buyers and sellers creates short-term price pressure. When buy-side aggression exceeds sell-side by a threshold, the order book tilts and market makers adjust their quotes upward. This creates a 15-45 second drift before the book rebalances as new limit orders arrive to capture the improved price.
weaknesses: Levels can 'blow through' during strong news
Requires high liquidity to exit at round numbers
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; apply to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index instead of FnO universe; stop/target recalibration for 5-second timeframe. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
